**That's the answer — and it fully vindicates your skepticism.** It was never floor slip:

| Command (from spawn) | Body moved | Turned |
|---|---|---|
| **FORWARD** (+x) | **0.012 m** ❌ blocked | 0.9° |
| **BACKWARD** (−x) | **2.208 m** ✅ | 0° |
| **ROTATE** | 0.000 m | **119°** ✅ |
| **FORWARD again** (after backing off) | **2.220 m** ✅ | 0° |

**Traction is perfect** — the body moves 2.2m backward, rotates freely, and drives 2.2m forward *once it's repositioned*. The **only** reason forward-from-spawn didn't move is that **the robot spawns nose-to-nose with its dock** (dock at x≈0.157, robot front at ~0.17) — every forward command I ran was pushing straight into the dock, wheels slipping against it. With the bump reflex now disabled, it just grinds there.

GuideMate sim on WSL2 ROS2 Jazzy + Gazebo, namespace robot_1. Step 1 (working sim) SOLVED 2026-07-04 after switching WSL to NAT — see [[guidemate-wsl-networking-nat-switch]].

Launch: `bash ~/robotics/sim_start.sh [world]` (default world=maze; also depot/warehouse). The script clears stale DDS env + `/dev/shm`, then runs `ros2 launch turtlebot4_gz_bringup turtlebot4_gz.launch.py namespace:=robot_1 rviz:=false world:=<world>`. **Run it in a dedicated terminal so the sim persists** (background launches via the agent die at session boundaries). Software rendering (LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1) → slow; diffdrive controller takes ~30s to activate.

Confirmed healthy in NAT mode: 0 SHM errors, `ros2` daemon works, scan + odom + cmd_vel all deliver, robot drives.

Key facts:
- Drive: publish `geometry_msgs/msg/Twist` to `/robot_1/cmd_vel_unstamped` (no timestamp check). (`/robot_1/cmd_vel` takes TwistStamped but needs a valid sim-time stamp; diffdrive use_stamped_vel=false, cmd_vel_timeout=0.5s drops stale msgs.)
- `/robot_1/odom` DOES exist (earlier note was wrong) — frame `robot_1/odom`, child `robot_1/base_link`; use it as the drive-response signal. Lidar: `/robot_1/scan` (640 ranges, frame `robot_1/turtlebot4/rplidar_link/rplidar`).
- **`/robot_1/sim_ground_truth_pose` is UNRELIABLE** (BEST_EFFORT + publishes on-change): goes SILENT when the robot is static, and is flaky even during motion. Do NOT rely on it for validation — use `/robot_1/odom` + lidar scene-change instead. (Dock GT pose is separate and steadier.)
- **TF is namespaced: `/robot_1/tf` (dynamic) + `/robot_1/tf_static` (latched, TRANSIENT_LOCAL — subscribe with matching durability or you get nothing).** Chain: `robot_1/odom`→(dyn)→`robot_1/base_link`→(static)→…→lidar. **No `base_footprint`** — base frame is `robot_1/base_link`. Static base→lidar = `[-0.04,0,0.193]` +90° yaw.
- **DRIVING GOTCHA:** robot ignores cmd_vel unless the create3 safety gate is off — see [[guidemate-create3-motion-control-drive-fix]]. Also: `/robot_1/cmd_vel` (TwistStamped) is dropped by diffdrive_controller if stamp is >0.5s old (RTF<1 makes this easy) — publish to `cmd_vel_unstamped` instead.
- **Loaded maze world = `turtlebot4_gz_bringup/worlds/maze.sdf`** (`<world name='maze'>`), NOT `irobot_create_gz_bringup/worlds/maze.sdf` (name 'default') — resource path puts turtlebot4 first. Editing the irobot_create copy is INERT.
- Nav2/AMCL bringup: use the TB4 wrapper `turtlebot4_navigation localization.launch.py` (adds PushRosNamespace); nav2_bringup's own launch does NOT namespace its nodes. Custom params `~/robotics/nav2/localization_maze.yaml` (frames prefixed robot_1/, global=map, set_initial_pose at origin); launcher `~/robotics/nav2/loc_start.sh`. AMCL verified: publishes map→robot_1/odom, 98% scan-on-wall. Comm-diag tools in `~/robotics/diag/`.
- Robot spawns UNDOCKED (dock_status is_docked:false) — no undock needed. Undock action exists at `/robot_1/undock` (irobot_create_msgs/action/Undock) if ever docked.
- Dark HMI LEDs are COSMETIC ONLY: turtlebot4_node needs create3 hardware services (start_motor, etc.) absent in sim, and the HMI GUI plugin's namespace is empty. Zero functional impact — ignore them; verify health by watching the robot move instead.
- Gazebo runs as `ruby` processes (comm=ruby), NOT `gz` — `pgrep`/`ps` for gazebo must account for that.
- No headless flag in stock launch (GUI hardcoded in sim.launch.py; turtlebot4_gz.launch.py does not forward gz_args). A custom launch is needed later for headless (`gz sim -s`) and faster-than-realtime (physics real_time_factor).
- Nav2 launchers: `turtlebot4_navigation` {nav2, localization, slam}.launch.py.
See [[guidemate-mvp-plan]].

Memory corrected. Here's the bottom line and where it leaves us.

## Resolved: the robot drives correctly
Your instinct was right that we hadn't proven it — and chasing it down revealed the truth: **traction is perfect, the robot drives 2.2m in every direction**. "Won't move" had two real, separate causes, both now understood:
1. **motion_control safety gate** — blocked commands → fixed (`safety_override: full`).
2. **Spawn pins the robot against its dock** — forward-from-spawn grinds into the dock; I only tested forward, so it masked cause #1's fix.

Neither is slip/friction/comms/physics. The comm suite separately proved the transport is clean. So the whole "robot won't move / GT not moving / bad odom-vs-truth" thread is genuinely closed — with the caveat that **odom is not a trustworthy displacement signal** (it races when wheels spin against the dock; GT at ~45Hz is the real arbiter).

## Implication for navigation (the one thing to handle)
The **dock is a real obstacle ~0.15m ahead of spawn**, and it's likely *not* in `maze_truth` (that map came from the world walls, not the dock model), and a 2D lidar at 0.19m height may under-see it. So before/at the first Nav2 goal we need **dock clearance** — cleanest options:
- **Undock action** (`/robot_1/undock`) to back the robot off first (realistic flow), or
- **Spawn offset** (the launch takes `x/y/yaw`) to start with clearance, or
- Let **Nav2 recovery** back it up (works, but messier for a first test).

I'd back it off first (undock or a scripted reverse), then send the goal — cleanest end-to-end proof.

**Recommended next step:** proceed to **Nav2 navigation bringup** — I'll build the nav params (same namespace/frame-prefix pattern as AMCL), get the robot dock-clear, and send one `NavigateToPose` goal so we watch it plan and drive there autonomously. Want me to start that?

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""GuideMate — send one NavigateToPose goal and monitor it end-to-end.

Picks a goal ~GOAL_DIST m from the robot's current pose that is FREE on
maze_truth (checked against the map), sends it to /robot_1/navigate_to_pose,
streams distance-remaining feedback, and reports the final GT vs goal error.
Usage: send_goal.py [gx gy]   (explicit world goal, else auto-pick a free one)
"""
import sys, math, time, yaml, numpy as np
import rclpy
from rclpy.node import Node
from rclpy.action import ActionClient
from rclpy.qos import qos_profile_sensor_data
from nav_msgs.msg import Odometry
from geometry_msgs.msg import PoseStamped
from nav2_msgs.action import NavigateToPose
from PIL import Image

BASE = '/home/baishibo123/robotics/maps/maze_truth'
y = yaml.safe_load(open(BASE + '.yaml'))
res = y['resolution']; ox, oy = y['origin'][0], y['origin'][1]
gray = np.array(Image.open(BASE + '.pgm').convert('L')); H, W = gray.shape

def free(wx, wy):
    """True if world point is free (light) on the map, with margin."""
    c = int((wx-ox)/res); r = int(H-(wy-oy)/res)
    if not (2 <= r < H-2 and 2 <= c < W-2): return False
    return bool((gray[r-4:r+5, c-4:c+5] > 250).all())  # 0.2m clear box

rclpy.init(); n = Node('send_goal')
s = {'g': None}
n.create_subscription(Odometry, '/robot_1/sim_ground_truth_pose',
                      lambda m: s.__setitem__('g', m.pose.pose), qos_profile_sensor_data)
e = time.monotonic()+10
while s['g'] is None and time.monotonic() < e: rclpy.spin_once(n, timeout_sec=0.05)
rx, ry = s['g'].position.x, s['g'].position.y
print(f"robot at ({rx:.2f},{ry:.2f})")

if len(sys.argv) >= 3:
    gx, gy = float(sys.argv[1]), float(sys.argv[2])
else:
    # auto-pick: scan rings/angles for a free point ~3m away
    gx = gy = None
    for dist in (3.0, 2.5, 2.0, 3.5, 1.5):
        for ang in range(0, 360, 15):
            a = math.radians(ang); cx, cy = rx+dist*math.cos(a), ry+dist*math.sin(a)
            if free(cx, cy): gx, gy = cx, cy; break
        if gx is not None: break
    if gx is None: print("no free goal found near robot"); rclpy.shutdown(); exit()
print(f"goal ({gx:.2f},{gy:.2f})  free_on_map={free(gx,gy)}  dist={math.hypot(gx-rx,gy-ry):.2f}m")

ac = ActionClient(n, NavigateToPose, '/robot_1/navigate_to_pose')
if not ac.wait_for_server(timeout_sec=15):
    print("navigate_to_pose action server not available"); rclpy.shutdown(); exit()

goal = NavigateToPose.Goal()
goal.pose.header.frame_id = 'map'
goal.pose.pose.position.x = gx; goal.pose.pose.position.y = gy
yaw = math.atan2(gy-ry, gx-rx)
goal.pose.pose.orientation.z = math.sin(yaw/2); goal.pose.pose.orientation.w = math.cos(yaw/2)

fb = {'last': None}
def on_fb(f): fb['last'] = f.feedback.distance_remaining
sgf = ac.send_goal_async(goal, feedback_callback=on_fb)
rclpy.spin_until_future_complete(n, sgf, timeout_sec=10)
gh = sgf.result()
if not gh or not gh.accepted:
    print("GOAL REJECTED"); rclpy.shutdown(); exit()
print("goal accepted — navigating...")
rf = gh.get_result_async()
t0 = time.monotonic(); last_print = 0
while not rf.done() and time.monotonic()-t0 < 180:
    rclpy.spin_once(n, timeout_sec=0.2)
    if time.monotonic()-last_print > 3 and fb['last'] is not None:
        g = s['g']
        print(f"  t={time.monotonic()-t0:5.0f}s  dist_remaining={fb['last']:.2f}m  "
              f"GT=({g.position.x:.2f},{g.position.y:.2f})")
        last_print = time.monotonic()
status = rf.result().status if rf.done() else None
g = s['g']; err = math.hypot(g.position.x-gx, g.position.y-gy)
# 4 = SUCCEEDED, 5 = CANCELED, 6 = ABORTED
names = {4: 'SUCCEEDED', 5: 'CANCELED', 6: 'ABORTED'}
print(f"RESULT: {names.get(status, status)}  final GT=({g.position.x:.2f},{g.position.y:.2f})  "
      f"error_to_goal={err:.2f}m")
rclpy.shutdown()

Status 2026-07-04: Step 1 (working TB4 Gazebo sim on the laptop) SOLVED. Building MVP #1 next.

**MVP #1 definition of done:** "In a headless DIY Gazebo world, publish a destination NAME (typed string via ROS topic/CLI) and one namespaced TB4 autonomously navigates there, faster-than-realtime, LIDAR-ONLY (no camera — privacy)."

**Locked decisions (Shibo):**
- Sim-only first (Jazzy); real Humble TB4 is a later port (TurtleBot4Navigator API differs).
- Command interface = local ROS topic + CLI now. AWS IoT/MQTT deferred (AWS IoT is just a cloud MQTT broker — unneeded for a single-laptop sim; wire it later as a transport in front of the same nav core).
- LLM/voice DEFERRED — typed string first, so the LLM workstream doesn't block the demo.
- No camera/image topics (privacy); lidar only.

**Why sim (Shibo's research angle):** stress-test coordination hardware can't — high-concurrency dispatch across many robots, and multi-robot cooperation/handoff (robot A escorts to floor-2 elevator, robot B takes over on floor 14). So MVP #1 is single-robot in behavior but **fleet-shaped in structure** from day one.

**Architecture (3 layers):** (1) Robot layer = per-robot namespaced Nav2 stack (namespace is already a launch arg, e.g. robot_1); (2) Dispatcher layer = fleet node that decides which robot handles a request (trivial for 1 robot now; the research-rich part later); (3) Input adapter layer = thin front-ends (CLI/topic now; MQTT/voice/LLM later) all calling the same nav core. Data model: destination `{name, floor, x, y, θ}` (include `floor` now, used later); floor/elevator topology graph = stub now.
